name: Kopkaka
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: van den Heuvel, Wilco & Sebastian Fedden. 2014. Greater Awyu and Greater Ok: inheritance or contact? Oceanic Linguistics 53(1): 1-36 (HAL hal-03950196 scan).
sources.note: Family-level only (text checked): p. 2 'While Mountain Ok languages are described as tonal (Telefol, Tifal, Mian), in Lowland Ok and Greater Awyu languages it is not the tone contour but lexical stress that seems to be distinctive'; p. ~18 (Muyu vs Mandobo) '..languages have distinctive lexical stress, as is true for all other [..] and some other Ok languages'. 'Kopkaka' occurs 0 times in the paper; not a Kopkaka statement.
Nothing; paywalled shell showing only classification (Trans-New Guinea > Ok-Awyu > Ok > Western) and alt. name Kopka.

sources.citation: de Vries, Lourens, Ruth Wester & Wilco van den Heuvel. 2012. The Greater Awyu language family of West Papua. Language & Linguistics in Melanesia Special Issue 2012 Part I: 269-312.
sources.note: Nothing. Kopkaka appears only in a subject-suffix comparison table ('Kopkaka (Kroneman 2010:11)') and the bibliography entry 'KRONEMAN, D. 2010 (unpublished manuscript). Kopkaka grammar sketch.'

sources.citation: Hughes, Jock. 2009. Upper Digul Survey. SIL ESR 2009-003; Lebold, Kriens, Sohn & Susanto. 2014. Report on the Upper Digul Helicopter Survey. SIL ESR 2014-002; Voorhoeve 1975 Languages of Irian Jaya (PL B-31).
sources.note: Nothing on Kopkaka: Hughes 2009 and Voorhoeve 1975 never mention Kopkaka/Seradela; Lebold et al. 2014 has 'KOPKAKA' only as a label on the survey map, no wordlist or text.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page kopk1238 and reference record 71719 (Wilbrink 2004).https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/kopk1238

The Kopkaka of Papua (MA thesis, VU Amsterdam, 219 pp., listed by Glottolog as a phonology, no URL/handle/DOI); other refs are van den Heuvel & Fedden 2014 (subclassification) and Campbell et al. 2022 ElCat (endangerment).

sources.citation: Badan Bahasa (Kemdikbud). Peta Bahasa: 'Kopkaka' entry idb=495.
sources.note: Indonesian national language-map entry cited by Wikipedia; Badan Bahasa entries occasionally summarise a field phonology; DNS failure at download time.

sources.note: Nothing. Phonology section is '[under construction]'; its only content is 'Wilbrink (2004: 29-58) gives 12 consonants and 5 vowels for Kopkaka of Seradela' with the inventory. Source inventory: Wilbrink (2004) 'phonology and grammar sketch' plus 209- and 837-term vocabularies of Seradela and comparative lists (pp. 97-110f); Kroneman (2010) 'grammar of Kopkaka'; Kroneman (n.d.) unpublished Unokob survey vocabulary. The words stress/accent/tone do not occur.

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. n.d. 'West Ok' and 'Ok' pages. Newguineaworld.https://newguineaworld.linguistik.uzh.ch/families/trans-new-guinea/central-west-new-guinea/digul-river-ok/ok/start
sources.note: Nothing on stress. West Ok page entirely under construction. Ok page: Proto-Ok historical phonology with Mountain Ok tones marked; Kopkaka appears only in a verbal subject-suffix table drawn from Kroneman (2010: 12-19); no Kopkaka forms with stress marks; 'stress'/'accent' absent.
Nothing; stub (villages Seredala, Moruf, Mosomduba, Burupmakot; dialects Tokuni, Marub, Kwer; refs Ethnologue 18, Peta Bahasa idb=495).
